RULE-SEC-001.title: Timing-Safe Webhook Signature Verification
RULE-SEC-001.statement: All incoming webhook signatures (Postmark, Stripe, Sentry, Lemon Squeezy) must be validated using constant-time comparison (crypto.timingSafeEqual) over raw request payloads to prevent side-channel timing attacks.
RULE-SEC-001.rationale: Prevents attacker ability to brute-force authentication signatures byte-by-byte via timing disparities.

RULE-SEC-002.title: Strict Public vs Private Secret Isolation
RULE-SEC-002.statement: Public client environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*) must never contain private API keys, backend server tokens, or decryption secrets.
RULE-SEC-002.rationale: Client bundles are fully accessible to end users; any leaked private secret compromises infrastructure.

RULE-SEC-003.title: Mandatory Telemetry & Error Data Scrubbing
RULE-SEC-003.statement: Before sending events to external observability or analytics providers (Sentry, Plausible, Umami, PostHog), payloads must pass through recursive data scrubbers stripping prompts, conversation transcripts, authorization headers, cookies, and user PII.
RULE-SEC-003.rationale: Protects user privacy and complies with data protection regulations while preventing prompt leakage.

RULE-SEC-004.title: No Raw Tokens in Commands, Transcripts, Files, or Shell History
RULE-SEC-004.statement: Authentication tokens, API keys, and bearer credentials must never be inlined in command-line arguments, tool invocations, conversation transcripts, source code, unencrypted files, or persistent shell history. Credential access must use OS keyring/credential managers (e.g., gh auth login), memory-zeroed SecureString pointers, or runtime environment variables with automated transcript scrubbing.
RULE-SEC-004.rationale: Inlined credentials permanently leak into shell history logs, process table listings (/proc, tasklist), CI logs, and agent transcript records, rendering prompt-level privacy guarantees moot.

RULE-WEB3-001.title: Soroban Stroop Precision & Decimal Drift Guard
RULE-WEB3-001.statement: All token mathematics and health factor calculations must maintain integer stroop precision (1e-7 tolerance) with deterministic remainder attribution to prevent decimal rounding losses or contract desync.
RULE-WEB3-001.rationale: Prevents cumulative rounding errors that could result in frozen funds or exploitable arbitrage.

RULE-WEB3-002.title: State Archival and TTL Extension Invariant
RULE-WEB3-002.statement: Every persistent or instance storage read/write in Soroban smart contracts must include TTL bump operations (MIN_TTL, BUMP_TTL) to prevent ledger archival of active contract data.
RULE-WEB3-002.rationale: Soroban state archiving deletes un-bumped data from active ledger state, breaking contract execution.

RULE-WEB3-003.title: Duplicate Settlement Anchoring Prevention
RULE-WEB3-003.statement: Settlement references and transaction hashes must map 1:1 with invoice/order records in persistent storage, returning explicit DuplicateSettlementRef errors on duplicate reuse attempts.
RULE-WEB3-003.rationale: Prevents double-spend and duplicate invoice settlement fraud across distinct payments.

RULE-MON-001.title: Strict 10,000 Basis Points (100.00%) Royalty Summation
RULE-MON-001.statement: Collaborator royalty splits must sum to exactly 10,000 basis points (100.00%) before contract submission, with pro-rata revenue calculated across individual recipients.
RULE-MON-001.rationale: Ensures all revenue is accounted for with zero unallocated leakage or over-allocation claims.
